CHAPTER IX
CONSULTATION & COORDINATION WITH OTHERS
Consultation in Preparation of this EIS
scripts.
Task Force— The Billings Area Office of the Bureau of Indian Affairs

(U.S. Department of the Interior) was responsible for preparation of
this draft EIS. As lead agency, the Billings Area Office, BIA, assembled a task force composed of the Project Leader and a number of disciplinary experts. Members of the task force were drawn from the
Billings Area Office, the BIA Planning Support Group, and various other
Federal agencies, in addition to members of the Crow Tribe of Indians.

Representatives of Westmoreland Resources, also assisted, and extensive use was made of consultants reports supplied by Westmoreland Resources concerning environmental baseline studies now in progress.

Other Federal Agencies— Various other Federal agencies provided technical data and expertise which greatly assisted in the timely preparation of this statement. These agencies also provided some review and commentary, and occasionally helped rewrite portions of the working manu-
The U. S. Geological Survey was directly involved in task force activities and contributed drafts concerning hydrology, mining operations, coal reserves, and geology. A separate USGS task force is currently preparing a draft EIS covering specifics of Westmoreland Resources proposed 20 year mining plan on Tract III. Through its members on the BIA task force, USGS members provided numerous charts and maps to support and clarify their written analyses. These people also reviewed various portions of the draft for technical accuracy and clarity.
